title: Tenant Resilience Synthetic Suite: Onboarding & Readiness Playbook
author: Aisha Khan
content:
Overview

This playbook describes the Tenant Resilience Synthetic Suite used during enterprise onboarding and the first-90-days readiness checks. The suite simulates realistic tenant workloads, cost-sensitive load patterns, and failure modes to verify SLO alignment, throttling behavior, and safe failback paths before and after go-live.

Goals

- Validate tenant-specific SLOs (p99 latency, error rate, and cost-per-1k-tokens) under realistic mixes.
- Confirm automatic fallback behavior (model variants, region/failover routing).
- Surface tenant-side cost sensitivity and quota protection thresholds.
- Produce artifacts for QBR: synthetic run report, drift signals, and remediation checklist.

When to run

1. Pre-cutover: complete nightly run for 3 consecutive days before scheduled cutover.
2. Post-cutover: hourly smoke runs during first 72 hours, then daily for first 30 days.
3. On-demand: after model upgrades, routing policy changes, or infra capacity events.

Prerequisites

- Customer tenant onboarded to test environment with production-like routing and telemetry keys.
- telemetry-gatekeeper integration completed and metrics forwarded to obs-dashboard.
- Access to synthetic-orchestrator project and API keys.

Suite Components

- Synthetic Orchestrator: coordinate workload scenarios, scale, and schedule.
- Traffic Templates: templates for text-gen streaming, embeddings bulk-index, and reranking bursts.
- Cost Sensitivity Harness: measures token spend vs latency and throttling.
- KV Cache Emulation: toggles warm/cold cache conditions to exercise cache hit behavior.
- Failure Injectors: network latency, dropped packets, model-serving errors, and GPU OOM triggers.
- Reporting Generator: produces PDF/JSON artifact for QBR and attaches to customer record.

Test Scenarios (recommended canonical set)

1) Baseline throughput profile
- Objective: establish stable p50/p95/p99 latency at nominal traffic for tenant commit.
- Load: 100 RPS steady (for small tenants) or tenant-specific baseline (derived from ingress estimate).
- Checks: p99 < SLO threshold, token cost within expected range (+/- 10%), 0 uncaught 5xx.

2) Spike + Quota Protection
- Objective: validate adaptive rate limiting and quota-protector webhook behavior.
- Load: ramp 10x for 60s, hold 5m, then decay.
- Expected: graceful 429s with quota header, no downstream cascades, telemetry annotation on rate-limit events.

3) Cold KV Cache Recovery
- Objective: ensure prefix/KV cache warming strategy keeps latency recovery under 2x baseline.
- Procedure: purge tenant cache, send burst of prefix-heavy requests, measure token-per-response and latency tail.

4) Model Fallback Simulation
- Objective: trigger primary model failure and verify fallback to compatible variant and alerting.
- Failure: synthetic-orchestrator flips a readiness flag on primary model instance.
- Expected: requests seamlessly routed to fallback, quality-safety gates log warnings, customer-facing latency within fallback SLO.

5) Cost Sensitivity Staircase
- Objective: quantify cost vs latency tradeoffs when changing batching and quantization profiles.
- Steps: run constant workload under three profiles: high-throughput (bigger batches), latency-first (smaller batches), quantized (int8).
- Report: delta cost per 1k tokens and quality regression notes.

Metrics & SLOs (example thresholds)

| Metric | SLO / Threshold | Operational Action |
|--------|-----------------|--------------------|
| p99 latency (token stream) | <= 800ms (Tier B) | If breached 3x in 10m, run canary rollback or throttle non-critical routes |
| 5xx rate | < 0.5% | Alert P1 if sustained > 1% for 5m |
| 429 rate (adaptive RL) | <= 2% | Verify quota-protector webhooks and notify CS if > 5% |
| Cost / 1k tokens | within +/- 15% of estimate | Trigger FinOps review if > +20% |
| KV cache hit rate | >= 65% after warmup | If < 40%, run cache-warm strategy and investigate prefix skews |

Runbook: executing a full suite run

1. Preparation (10–30 min):
   - Confirm tenant staging mapping and that ingress-gateway points at synthetic-orchestrator.
   - Check obs-dashboard baseline dash for last 24h.
   - Notify stakeholders (CS lead, customer-eng, infra-owner) via the go-live Slack channel.

2. Kickoff:
   - Start baseline scenario and verify health checks pass.
   - Start cost-sensitivity harness sequentially; do not run quantized profile concurrently with other heavy tests.

3. Monitoring during run:
   - Watch p99/p95/p50 in obs-dashboard.
   - Watch synthetic orchestrator logs for dropped requests and failures.
   - Confirm telemetry events include tags: tenant_id, synthetic_run_id, scenario_name.

4. Post-run artifact generation (automated):
   - Reporting generator emits report to /customer-records/<tenant>/synthetic-reports/<run-id>.pdf and JSON.

Automated checks & alert mapping

- If p99 > threshold for > 5m -> alert ops-sre channel and create Incident stub with "synthetic-resilience" template.
- If cost / 1k tokens deviates by > 20% -> notify FinOps and CS; attach cost-sensitivity CSV.
- If fallback triggered -> send structured webhook to customer and open a follow-up ticket in Jira (label: synthetic-fallback).

Triage & Remediation Playbook (priority ladder)

1) Latency tail increases (p99 breach)
   - Check KV cache warmup metrics. If cold, execute cache-warm run using prefix-replay tool.
   - If cache healthy, throttle non-essential routes and escalate to eng-serving-runtime.

2) Elevated 5xx errors
   - Look for OOMs on GPU hosts; if present, mark node and trigger node-drain.
   - If errors originate from tenant proxy, roll forward to next stable tenant-proxy commit or apply immediate rollback.

3) Unexpected cost spike
   - Pause quantized/large-batch scenarios. Re-run small-sample to confirm.
   - Attach run trace to FinOps review and propose batch-sizing or model-variant changes.

4) Fallback quality concerns
   - Compare prompt-set evals captured during run. If regression > configured threshold, add to model-onboarding backlog and schedule immediate rollback to pre-upgrade pin.

Post-onboarding artifacts to produce

- Synthetic Run report (PDF + JSON) with: scenario definitions, raw telemetry links, SLO compliance badges, and remediation tasks.
- Tenant Resilience Checklist (signed-off by CS and infra).
- QBR short brief (1 page) highlighting: stability score, cost variance, and known open remediation items.

Ownership & escalation

- Primary owner: customer-success (Aisha Khan).
- Secondary owners: eng-serving-runtime (on-call rotation), eng-sre (capacity and infra remediation).
- Escalation path: CS -> Infra Pager -> Eng SRE lead -> Oncall Eng Serving Runtime -> Product PM (for model/variant decisions).

Frequently asked questions

Q: What if synthetic runs pass but production diverges?
A: Confirm traffic parity (routing weights), client prompt differences, and dataset split. Schedule a focused production-sampling run with lower-fidelity sampling to identify prompt drift.

Q: Can the suite run against Dedicated / Private tenants?
A: Yes. For Private deployments, use local synthetic-orchestrator deployment and ensure you run within customer's air-gapped testing window. Coordinate with Private deployment owner for network allowances.

  ],

CLI quick checks

- Start a run: curl -X POST "https://synthetic-orchestrator.internal/api/v1/runs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SYNTH_KEY" -d '@scenario.json'
- Fetch run status: curl "https://synthetic-orchestrator.internal/api/v1/runs/<run-id>/status"
